entry.description: On Zeros and Algorithms for Disordered Systems II: The Antiferromagnetic Ising Model up to Kesten-Stigum. The primary source reports: We give the first polynomial-time algorithm to estimate the partition function of the antiferromagnetic Ising model on the uniformly random d d -regular graph to arbitrarily high accuracy for all inverse temperatures up to the Kesten–Stigum threshold. This is the entire regime in which the model is “replica symmetric”, and is conjectured to be optimal for polynomial-time counting and sampling. To achieve our algorithmic result, we establish the absence of Fisher zeros for the partition function in a constant-width strip around the interval from 0 0 up to the Kesten–Stigum threshold, with high probability over the randomness of the input graph. AI Disclosure The overarching vision and proof architecture were developed solely by the authors without AI input. GPT 5.5 Pro was used, with extensive guidance from the authors, for only a few minor technical aspects of the proof. The authors independently verified correctness and wrote everything by hand. We take full responsibility for its contents. A more detailed statement can be found in Section 1.2 . Direct AI involvement: Primary paper disclosure (source-attributed excerpts): ration estimates, etc. The authors independently verified the correctness of all arguments in the paper, and take full responsibility for its contents. The authors initially attempted to have GPT 5.6 Codex help merge several handwritten/hand-typed notes containing various pieces of the proof into a single cohesive document. The result was very far from satisfactory, so the entirety of the paper was written and checked manually. Independent Work Recently, Chen–Wang–Zhang independently proved Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 and extended them to the hardcore model and the q q -state antiferromagnetic Potts models on random d d -regular graphs. Their proof also uses the second moment method and small subgraph conditioning, applied to a suitable truncation of the partition function. However, they are able to avoid the use of Jensen’s Formula and analytic reweighting by using the method of tightness , a strategy first implemented (to the best of our knowledge) by [ 14 ] in the context of random matrix theory. We thank Sidhanth Mohanty for pointing out this reference. 1.3 Prior Work Worst-Case Approximate  Further checking: AI used for routine moment/concentration proof calculations only; architecture is human and rejected Codex draft was not retained. entry.description: Near-Null Limits and Contact Distributions for Maxwell Composite Operators. The primary source reports: We investigate the simultaneous near-null, longitudinal-continuum, and ultraviolet limits of four-point correlation functions of quadratic composite operators in Maxwell theory. Taking the external momenta to be collinear and spacelike, we weight each loop integral by a smooth test function of the routed longitudinal momentum. All three connected Wick contraction cycles are generated from a common Gaussian source functional and regulated by a cutoff on the total proper time. For the resulting integrals restricted to a fixed ultraviolet proper-time interval, we establish the uniform bound ∣ I δ , M ϵ [ ϕ ] − I 0 , ∞ ϵ [ ϕ ] ∣ ≤ C ∥ ϕ ∥ C b 8 ( δ ϵ − 3 + M − 2 δ − 3 ϵ − 1 ) \left|\mathcal I_{\delta,M}^{\epsilon}[\phi]-\mathcal I_{0,\infty}^{\epsilon}[\phi]\right|\le C\|\phi\|_{C_b^8}\left(\delta\epsilon^{-3}+M^{-2}\delta^{-3}\epsilon^{-1}\right) ​ I δ , M ϵ ​ [ ϕ ] − I 0 , ∞ ϵ ​ [ ϕ ] ​ ≤ C ∥ ϕ ∥ C b 8 ​ ​ ( δ ϵ − 3 + M − 2 δ − 3 ϵ − 1 ) , where δ \delta δ denotes the dimensionless near-null tilt parameter and M M M specifies the longitudinal lattice resolution. This estimate determines the joint scaling regimes under which a universal counterterm subtraction yields an identical renormalized finite part. We further show that the longitudinal logarithmic divergence of the alternating chiral cycle is governed by the measure 81 ( 0 , 1 ) d ξ + 3 δ 0 + 3 δ 1 8\mathbf 1_{(0,1)}\mathrm d\xi+3\delta_0+3\delta_1 8 1 ( 0 , 1 ) ​ d ξ + 3 δ 0 ​ + 3 δ 1 ​ , whereas each of the other two cycles contributes 81 ( 0 , 2 ) d ξ 8\mathbf 1_{(0,2)}\mathrm d\xi 8 1 ( 0 , 2 ) ​ d ξ . These distributional coefficients emerge from the complete covariant numerators, including the instantaneous longitudinal terms. Finally, for the alternating cycle and any smooth compactly supported test function coinciding with ξ 2 \xi^2 ξ 2 in a neighborhood of [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] [ 0 , 1 ] , the critical trajectory δ = c ϵ 3 \delta=c\epsilon^3 δ = c ϵ 3 with M 2 δ 3 ϵ → ∞ M^2\delta^3\epsilon\to\infty M 2 δ 3 ϵ → ∞ leaves a finite discrepancy of 30 c 30c 30 c , demonstrating the sharpness of the tilt scaling. entry.description: Computing Jacobsthal’s Function on Primorials: Exact Values and Constructive Bounds. The primary source reports: Let h(x) = j(Px), where j is Jacobsthal’s function and Px is the product of the first x primes. We describe a parallel residue-covering search. Exhaustive exclusion runs, together with independently checked covering witnesses, establish h(65) = 1134, h(66) = 1160, h(67) = 1192, h(68) = 1216, h(69) = 1248, h(70) = 1274, and h(71) = 1298. Method 5B gives explicit certificates for h(100) ≥ 2054, h(150) ≥ 3558, and h(200) ≥ 5172, using partial coverings with five reserve primes. Exhaustive searches give h(100) ≤ 2798, h(150) ≤ 6898, and h(200) ≤ 11998. The search combines parity compression, descending endpoint restrictions, canonical deduplication, a sliding-window bootstrap, and dynamic prime selection related to Ziller and Morack’s Greedy Permutation Algorithm. We state the conditions needed for capacity bounds and conditional propagation, and organize extensions of complete or partial coverings in a five-tier framework. A catalog of 62 coverings at index 65 supports a verified multi-certificate envelope. The solver source, run evidence, certificates, and arithmetic verifiers are publicly available in the accompanying GitHub release v1.0-paper. entry.description: A two-sided criterion for the Riemann hypothesis from weighted prime sums, verified up to 2·10^29. The primary source reports: For N > 1 let C(N) = 2 Σ_{n<N} Λ(n) n^{-1/2} log(N/n) and M(N) = R(N) − C(N), where R(N) = 8√N − 5.3721834 log N − 7.4013354 + O(N^{-5/2}) is explicit. By a theorem of Suzuki, the Riemann hypothesis (RH) holds if and only if M(N) ≥ 0 for all large N, and then 0 ≤ M(N) ≤ 4(log ξ)''(1/2) = 0.18484. We prove, with computer assistance, that this two-sided inequality holds for every real 1 < N ≤ 2.15·10^29: up to 10^10 from the primes with correctly rounded arithmetic, and beyond from the first 4520 zeros, certified with ball arithmetic, together with the verification of RH to 3·10^12 and an explicit zero-density estimate. The same ingredients give, for every N and without any hypothesis, −E(N) ≤ M(N) ≤ 0.18484 + E(N) with E(N) explicit and E(10^20) < 3·10^-5. We describe the local minima of M exactly and prove an unconditional energy identity for the slope α(x) = Σ_{n≤x} Λ(n) n^{-1/2} − 2√x + c0/2. We then show that positive weights within q^{δ−1/2} of Λ(q) q^{-1/2} satisfy the energy identity, the prime number theorem and Chebyshev’s identity, yet carry an off-line zero, so any proof must use Λ = μ∗log exactly. We do not prove the Riemann hypothesis. entry.description: Maximal Independent Sets in Long Graph Subdivisions. The primary source reports: We study maximal independent sets in finite simple graphs whose edges are replaced by paths with prescribed numbers of internal vertices. Using established finite-state transfer methods, we derive an exact boundary-state formula and an explicit leading asymptotic term that factors over the degrees of the original vertices. A graph-uniform relative error bound gives a sufficient condition for this approximation to remain valid when the base graph grows. Under the same condition, the joint membership indicators of the original vertices approach an explicit product of Bernoulli distributions in total variation. For fixed base graphs, we obtain the first adjacency-sensitive correction and a Gaussian limit for the size of a uniformly chosen maximal independent set. A degree-matched construction demonstrates that bounded aggregate error scale does not suffice for uniform degree-sequence universality. Reproducibility materials include exact enumeration, weighted and moment checks, and numerical spectral comparisons. Direct AI involvement: Daniel A. Pyle initiated this research project. OpenAI AI systems performed the technical derivations, computational checks, manuscript drafting, and internal review under his direction. The work builds on established finite-state transfer methods and the literature cited in the manuscript. The manuscript has not been peer reviewed or formally verified, and originality remains subject to further literature review. entry.description: A Linear In Rank Bound For Integral Arithmetic Progressions On Elliptic Curves. The primary source reports: Every known bound on the length N of an x-progression on an elliptic curve of rank r has the shape N ≤ C^{1+r}. We prove a bound that is linear in the rank for integral progressions, with an error depending only on the height of the model. Let y^2 = x^3 +a_2x^2 +a_4x+a_6 be an integral model and H_f = 1+|a2|+|a4|+|a6|. For every ε > 0, every integral x-progression of length N satisfies N ≤ (3/2 +ε)s+C_{ε} (1+log(H_f))^{1/2}, where s ≤ r is the rank of the span of the progression. In particular N ≤ (3/2 +o(1))s whenever log H_f = o(N^2). The proof has two halves. The local theory consists of exact point counts, the root-class lemma, pinned values, and a forbidden range of primes reaching N^2/49 by a shift-and-square argument. It forces log |b| ≫ N^2, where b is the common difference. The spectral cap is proved in an exact form. Splitting the Neron–Tate pairing into local kernels of positive type and summing the regularised diagonal terms over all places gives an identity in which the bad-prime corrections cancel. Combined with a uniform archimedean separation lemma, this yields λ_{max}(G) ≤ (3/4) logX + (1/4) ψ(N − 1) + (5/4) log(H_f )+ 2, where X =max|x_i|. entry.description: First-order phase transition in Onsager's model of hard rods in $\mathbb R^3$. The primary source reports: We prove a first-order transition for hard rods in R 3 \mathbb R^3 R 3 whose orientations vary continuously over the sphere. For every sufficiently small positive ratio of diameter to length, the grand-canonical pressure has a nondifferentiable point, with a jump in number density at the intermediate Onsager scale. Following the phase-pressure strategy of Lebowitz, Mazel, and Presutti, we connect coexistence in the homogeneous Onsager functional to the microscopic pressure through an exact auxiliary-field representation, exponential decay of correlations in the rod gas at fixed auxiliary field, and estimates of the free-energy cost of interfaces between connected families of minimizing angular profiles. Direct AI involvement: Astra was prompted to prove the existence of a first-order phase transition for the hard-rod model in the three-dimensional continuum, either via the analytic route by proving the non-differentiability of its thermodynamic potential, or via the probabilistic route by proving the coexistence of a continuum of Gibbs measures. It chose the analytic route and produced a candidate proof in an essentially zero-shot run lasting about six hours, with occasional interruptions due to connection errors. The argument closely resembled the work of Lebowitz, Mazel, and Presutti (1999) on the existence of a liquid-vapor transition in a continuum model. Astra was then directed to make these connections explicit and, more broadly, give appropriate credit to the existing literature. It seems that, in working directly with the grand-canonical pressure, Astra has cleverly circumvented the need to prove continuous symmetry breaking. ***THE RESULT IS NOT HUMAN-VERIFIED*** Further checking: Pressure nondifferentiability/density jump for sufficiently thin rods; not a claimed proof of continuous symmetry breaking. It seems that, in working directly with the grand-canonical pressure, Astra has cleverly circumvented the need to prove continuous symmetry breaking. ***THE RESULT IS NOT HUMAN-VERIFIED***

A hypothetical 29 29 29 -block cover has at least five points lying in exactly 15 15 15 blocks. The link at one of these points leaves only 14 14 14 blocks outside it. entry.description: Finite Alphabet Communication with Noisy Forward Memory in a Normalized Loop. The primary source reports: We study one-use communication of a finite classical message through a stipulated normalized loop containing a backward binary symmetric channel and one noisy forward memory carrier. The carrier is either a classical bit or a qubit; no shared random seed, retained side register, or entanglement is supplied. For every finite message count, we characterize the qubit optimum by a constructive scalar feasibility test. For rational noise parameters and a rational target success, the test uses O(M²) constant-size rational arithmetic checks. The proof combines an exact decoder reduction, minimum-trace allocation for constant encoders, and a concave geometric cap with a matching polygon construction. For three messages, the qubit and classical-bit optima coincide throughout the allowed noise range; an explicit Bernstein certificate proves the remaining polynomial inequality. For four messages, an exact rational qubit protocol exceeds a bound valid for every classical-bit protocol. These are conditional mathematical results for the declared resource model, not a construction of a physical backward channel. Independent human review and originality assessment remain pending. Direct AI involvement: This manuscript was prepared through an AI-assisted research workflow. Lyra, an OpenAI AI assistant, carried out the technical derivations, computational verification, literature checking, and manuscript drafting under Daniel A. Pyle’s direction. Independent human proof review and a fuller originality assessment remain pending. The results concern a stipulated mathematical model and do not establish physical backward communication. entry.description: Smallest Gaps between Eigenvalues of Wigner Matrices without Smoothness Assumptions. The primary source reports: We determine the asymptotic distribution of the smallest gaps between eigenvalues in the bulk of the spectrum of real symmetric Wigner matrices, including Bernoulli matrices. After multiplication by N 3 / 2 N^{3/2} N 3/2 , the gaps and their locations converge to a Poisson point process with the same intensity as for the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble. Since changing a single entry can move eigenvalues by an amount comparable to the smallest gaps, standard perturbative comparison estimates do not directly resolve this scale for arbitrary entry distributions. Instead, we use that resampling a few random entries does not change the law of the matrix, and we show that the resampling moves each pair of nearby eigenvalues by a random walk that satisfies a local limit theorem; this requires excluding arithmetic structure in the eigenvectors. We also prove a law of large numbers for the number of gaps at all scales between N − 3 / 2 N^{-3/2} N − 3/2 and N − 1 N^{-1} N − 1 , and we sketch the proof of the analogous smallest-gap result for complex Hermitian Wigner matrices. Direct AI involvement: Proof discovery, verification, and writing were done with GPT 6 Astra, GPT 6.1 Sol, and Claude Opus 5.5. entry.description: Arithmetic Expression Spaces: Expansion and Motion, Eikonal Equation, Horocycle Pullbacks, Commutativization, Contact Structure, and Tearing. The primary source reports: An arithmetic expression is a word of operations; a motion is a flow on a manifold. For expressions whose evaluation has a single internal spine, the two are one structure: affine for addition and multiplication, projective once the second operand slot is divided, contact-geometric in the order defect. A regular arithmetic expression space (AES) is an oriented Riemannian surface ( M , g ) (M,g) ( M , g ) with a smooth assignment a ⁣ : M → R a\colon M\to\mathbb R a : M → R satisfying the eikonal equation ∣ ∇ a ∣ g 2 = μ 2 + λ 2 a 2 |\nabla a|_g^2=\mu^2+\lambda^2a^2 ∣∇ a ∣ g 2 ​ = μ 2 + λ 2 a 2 ; the four operations then act as motions translating and scaling a a a . In the basic model E 0 \mathfrak E_0 E 0 ​ , the upper half-plane with the left-invariant metric of A f f + ( 1 , R ) \mathrm{Aff}^+(1,\mathbb R) Aff + ( 1 , R ) (curvature − λ 2 -\lambda^2 − λ 2 ), addition and positive multiplication are affine translations and dilations obeying a Baumslag--Solitar law, and a a a is a Laplace--Beltrami eigenfunction of eigenvalue 2 λ 2 2\lambda^2 2 λ 2 . Left-expanded words stay in the affine Borel cell fixing ∞ \infty ∞ ; the right-expanded language, once second-slot division is admitted, generates all of P G L 2 ( R ) \mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb R) PGL 2 ​ ( R ) through the rank-one Bruhat decomposition, and pulling standard horocycles back along one operator word gives the dual reading, ripple geometry. Commutativizing the motions by total charge yields the accumulative commutative space, where the order defect of two histories is an exact weighted area, the tearing. The same defect is the constant μ λ \mu\lambda μ λ in the bracket [ D u , D v ] = μ λ ∂ a [D_u,D_v]=\mu\lambda\partial_a [ D u ​ , D v ​ ] = μ λ ∂ a ​ of the horizontal fields of α = d a − μ d u − λ a d v \alpha=da-\mu\,du-\lambda a\,dv α = d a − μ d u − λa d v , a contact form whenever μ λ ≠ 0 \mu\lambda\ne0 μ λ  = 0 , and it is the curvature of that horizontal connection; for E 0 \mathfrak E_0 E 0 ​ the basic model is proved to be the Reeb quotient of the contact model, and fixed-charge tearing and fixed-state Reeb drift are Legendre dual readings of the same curvature. The generators ∂ a \partial_a ∂ a ​ , a ∂ a a\partial_a a ∂ a ​ , and a log ⁡ a ∂ a a\log a\,\partial_a a lo g a ∂ a ​ span an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra, so no finite-dimensional Lie group carries all three ranks, and no observable of the charge endpoint detects tearing. GitHub account ownership, CI success and mergeability are not independent review. ## Historical weekly provenance register: 2026-10-12 through 2026-10-18 The dispositions below are snapshots at 2026-10-18; later acceptance is recorded separately, without rewriting the historical findings. ### P-2026-10-18-07 — Finite process spectra and cyclic-prefix separation - **Human origin/direction:** Mingli Yuan selected the process-spectrum, Alexandrov reconstruction and finite-observation questions and retains final acceptance and release authority. - **Model assistance:** Codex (OpenAI) supplied the finite constructions, proofs, enumeration, executable receivers, mutation controls and prose. - **Objectification:** Draft PR [#17](https://github.com/mountain/aeg-paper/pull/17), head `e4d51425ccfa3575c87f5bd7a9d66cbb4128ee16`. - **Result:** the three-event chain and fork have equal undirected cover Laplacian spectra but different causal orders and Alexandrov lower opens; all 19 labelled three-element posets reconstruct in the declared finite route. The guarded loop/stopping pair shares each prescribed finite packet prefix, while terminal status separates them. - **Boundary:** no general rejection of spectral methods, infinite-run certificate or Adva anytime theorem. - **Human disposition:** retained Draft/Open; explicit approval of the final reviewed head and independent human mathematical review are absent. - **Status:** `draft-bounded-result`. ### P-2026-10-18-08 — Process-representation gap programme - **Human origin/direction:** Mingli Yuan selected the representation-gap work plan, process-geometric questions and final publication boundary. - **Model assistance:** AI systems implemented the six frozen experiments, replay and red-team review. The original producing-model identity is not consistently fixed in the initial commit record and remains a provenance gap; the review is model cross-checking, not independent human review. - **Objectification:** PR [#18](https://github.com/mountain/aeg-paper/pull/18), reviewed head `1556eaedaee0946b2e395320739234dc59ec846c`. - **Reproduced finite evidence:** braid representation counts `5461 -> 1457 -> 577 -> 6`, the bounded separating probe and 20 moving-obstacle interval certificates. - **Blocking corrections:** both self-embedding checkers accept a triangle that collapses at `t=1/2`; the committed R2 fixture violates necessary planar Gauss parity; the strict-torus nontrivial-knot exclusion is false; and the freeze guard can refresh existing contract digests. Green replay CI therefore does not establish mathematical correctness. - **Review disposition at 2026-10-18:** model review required changes; no merge or theorem promotion was recorded. - **Status:** reproducible experiment with explicit `rejected-or-unknown` mathematical/verification blockers. ## Subsequent acceptance and repairs — 2026-10-19 UTC Mingli Yuan explicitly requested merging all open aeg-paper PRs into main in this session. This authorizes repository integration; it does not establish independent human mathematical review or promote a finite result to a theorem. - **PR #17:** merged as `b75b0cbe17fc8a7417a8db9c392f33109f04a80a` after normal/optimized producer and independent-receiver replay matched frozen evidence. The exact reviewed head's Paper 0/I/IV integration and PDF build workflow succeeded. Its bounded-result and native-Adva limitations remain. - **PR #18 repair direction:** restrict positive motion certification to verified rigid translations; retain the historical R1/R2-named operations as abstract signed-word calculations; withdraw planar Reidemeister and knot-process faithfulness claims. Correct sphere/torus and framing statements. - **PR #18 model contribution:** Codex (OpenAI) implemented the two narrowed embedding routes, geometry and integrity regressions, immutable historical contract pins, explicit replay inventory, temporary-output replay and fresh raw-table comparison, and drafted the corrected reports. The original producing-model provenance gap remains recorded above. - **Repair identities:** v1.1 contract `7600707e3b9a98a37cfde325464b260b9a2c36a8`; implementation `0697b1ca0eb85f4383811f23534e78af19191d8e`; integrated candidate `fdead22a64f3ece04778c598f32df92001e8031e`. - **Preservation:** original v1 contracts and rejection-review artifacts remain unchanged. Historical reports, evidence and fixtures are indexed by exact commit/blob/SHA-256 in `research/process-representation-gap/reviews/2026-10-19-repair-history.json`. Current exp6 evidence is an explicit v1.1 successor. - **Acceptance boundary:** documentary research integration only. General motion certification, planar local-move certification and native Adva continuation/learning integration remain open; no manuscript theorem changes. ## Contribution interpretation Mingli Yuan is the human research director, acceptance and release authority, and final human scientific responsibility holder. Model contributions must be named per commit/PR when known and must not be reassigned to the GitHub account holder. Model cross-review is not independent human review.

GitHub account ownership, CI success and mergeability are not independent review. ## Historical weekly provenance register: 2026-10-12 through 2026-10-18 The dispositions below are snapshots at 2026-10-18; later acceptance is recorded separately, without rewriting the historical findings. ### P-2026-10-18-07 — Finite process spectra and cyclic-prefix separation - **Human origin/direction:** Mingli Yuan selected the process-spectrum, Alexandrov reconstruction and finite-observation questions and retains final acceptance and release authority. - **Model assistance:** Codex (OpenAI) supplied the finite constructions, proofs, enumeration, executable receivers, mutation controls and prose. - **Objectification:** Draft PR [#17](https://github.com/mountain/aeg-paper/pull/17), head `e4d51425ccfa3575c87f5bd7a9d66cbb4128ee16`. - **Result:** the three-event chain and fork have equal undirected cover Laplacian spectra but different causal orders and Alexandrov lower opens; all 19 labelled three-element posets reconstruct in the declared finite route. The guarded loop/stopping pair shares each prescribed finite packet prefix, while terminal status separates them. - **Boundary:** no general rejection of spectral methods, infinite-run certificate or Adva anytime theorem. - **Human disposition:** retained Draft/Open; explicit approval of the final reviewed head and independent human mathematical review are absent. - **Status:** `draft-bounded-result`. ### P-2026-10-18-08 — Process-representation gap programme - **Human origin/direction:** Mingli Yuan selected the representation-gap work plan, process-geometric questions and final publication boundary. - **Model assistance:** AI systems implemented the six frozen experiments, replay and red-team review. The original producing-model identity is not consistently fixed in the initial commit record and remains a provenance gap; the review is model cross-checking, not independent human review. - **Objectification:** PR [#18](https://github.com/mountain/aeg-paper/pull/18), reviewed head `1556eaedaee0946b2e395320739234dc59ec846c`. - **Reproduced finite evidence:** braid representation counts `5461 -> 1457 -> 577 -> 6`, the bounded separating probe and 20 moving-obstacle interval certificates. - **Blocking corrections:** both self-embedding checkers accept a triangle that collapses at `t=1/2`; the committed R2 fixture violates necessary planar Gauss parity; the strict-torus nontrivial-knot exclusion is false; and the freeze guard can refresh existing contract digests. Green replay CI therefore does not establish mathematical correctness. - **Review disposition at 2026-10-18:** model review required changes; no merge or theorem promotion was recorded. - **Status:** reproducible experiment with explicit `rejected-or-unknown` mathematical/verification blockers. ## Subsequent acceptance and repairs — 2026-10-19 UTC Mingli Yuan explicitly requested merging all open aeg-paper PRs into main in this session. This authorizes repository integration; it does not establish independent human mathematical review or promote a finite result to a theorem. - **PR #17:** merged as `b75b0cbe17fc8a7417a8db9c392f33109f04a80a` after normal/optimized producer and independent-receiver replay matched frozen evidence. The exact reviewed head's Paper 0/I/IV integration and PDF build workflow succeeded. Its bounded-result and native-Adva limitations remain. - **PR #18 repair direction:** restrict positive motion certification to verified rigid translations; retain the historical R1/R2-named operations as abstract signed-word calculations; withdraw planar Reidemeister and knot-process faithfulness claims. Correct sphere/torus and framing statements. - **PR #18 model contribution:** Codex (OpenAI) implemented the two narrowed embedding routes, geometry and integrity regressions, immutable historical contract pins, explicit replay inventory, temporary-output replay and fresh raw-table comparison, and drafted the corrected reports. The original producing-model provenance gap remains recorded above. - **Repair identities:** v1.1 contract `7600707e3b9a98a37cfde325464b260b9a2c36a8`; implementation `0697b1ca0eb85f4383811f23534e78af19191d8e`; integrated candidate `fdead22a64f3ece04778c598f32df92001e8031e`. - **Preservation:** original v1 contracts and rejection-review artifacts remain unchanged. Historical reports, evidence and fixtures are indexed by exact commit/blob/SHA-256 in `research/process-representation-gap/reviews/2026-10-19-repair-history.json`. Current exp6 evidence is an explicit v1.1 successor. - **Acceptance boundary:** documentary research integration only. General motion certification, planar local-move certification and native Adva continuation/learning integration remain open; no manuscript theorem changes. ## Contribution interpretation Mingli Yuan is the human research director, acceptance and release authority, and final human scientific responsibility holder. entry.description: An exact computer-assisted certificate for R(5,6)≤84. The primary source reports: We give an exact computer-assisted proof of R(5,6)≤84. We derive a system of linear inequalities that must be satisfied by any graph on 84 vertices containing neither a five-vertex clique nor a six-vertex independent set. We provide explicit nonnegative rational weights for which adding these inequalities yields a contradiction. Published small Ramsey bounds and complete catalogues of smaller Ramsey graphs supply the external inputs. The accompanying verification programs check the derivation of the inequalities and their weighted sum using exact arithmetic. entry.description: Cyclic reductions of elliptic curves at a positive proportion of primes. The primary source reports: We prove that every elliptic curve over $\Q$ whose points of order two are not all rational has cyclic reduction at a positive lower density of primes. This is the only necessary restriction: full rational two-torsion prevents cyclic reduction at every odd prime of good reduction. More precisely, a common zero-free half-plane ℜ s > 1 − 1 / N \Re s>1-1/N ℜ s > 1 − 1/ N for Dedekind zeta functions gives a lower proportion of at least c E / ( N log ⁡ N ) c_E/(N\log N) c E ​ / ( N lo g N ) , with c E > 0 c_E>0 c E ​ > 0 independent of N N N ; the theorem of Cureton and Thorner supplies N = 32 N=32 N = 32 . The proof uses the varying-cofactor sieve of our earlier works on primitive roots and primitive points, in conjunction with the marked Type~II estimates of~OpenAI, to construct candidate primes. We then apply a smoothed explicit formula for Dedekind zeta functions, with nonnegative weights on prime ideals, to bound the number of candidates with noncyclic reduction. This gives a common argument for CM and non-CM curves. Direct AI involvement: Building on the techniques of [1] and [2], this paper shows that every elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ without full rational 2-torsion has cyclic reduction modulo a positive proportion of primes. The argument was worked out in handwritten notes, which were then converted into LaTeX, with additional writing and details added by both the author and GPT-6. The deduction of Theorems 1 and 2 from specified analytic and arithmetic inputs was then formalized in Lean with the help of GPT-6. The development proves the construction of the arithmetic progression, that every candidate prime with noncyclic reduction splits completely in some division field $K_\ell$ with $Y<\ell\le x^{\epsilon}$, the bound and subtraction of these exceptional primes, and the final lower proportion $c_E/(N\log N)$ with its specialization at $N=32$. The Cureton–Thorner zero-free hypothesis, candidate-prime estimate (Proposition 6), smoothed prime-ideal bound, prime number theorem, elementary prime-sum estimates, and standard facts about torsion, reduction, and division fields remain explicit hypotheses, and are described explicitly in the write up; their proofs were not formalized here. entry.description:
Maximality of the Došen–Petrić Boolean Category. The primary source reports: Let P be a nonempty set of propositional variables. The freely generated zero-identity Boolean category B(P) of Došen and Petrić is maximal: every congruence on its arrows preserved by the arrow operations and uniform formula substitution is either equality or identifies every pair of parallel arrows. The formalization gives two proofs of maximality and proves the congruence dichotomy. It also proves that the identity and zero endomorphism of each variable are distinct, and that there is no arrow from the terminal object to the initial object. Direct AI involvement: {"methods": [{"method": "agent", "models": [], "framework": "OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT", "tool_setup": "Local WSL Codex developed Lean proofs and ran builds and audits. ChatGPT research/review sessions prepared mathematical instructions, inspected source and evidence, and reviewed the manuscript and its correspondence with the formal statements. Exact historical model identifiers and aggregate costs are not reconstructed here."}], "notes": "Florian Lengyel is the human author and responsible maintainer. The author supplied the mathematical objective, corrected scope and presentation, and requested the complete-paper formalization. AI systems are credited here rather than listed as authors. The manuscript contains the author's authorized disclosure of ChatGPT assistance."} Further checking: Check source/repository first-public chronology and overlap with the full corpus. The three maximality declarations retain the manuscript's nonempty-variable hypothesis. PrimitiveCongruence is an equivalence relation on parallel typed arrow terms that contains every defining equation and is preserved by composition, conjunction and disjunction. Its Closed property requires preservation under uniform formula substitution on the terms and both endpoints. Derives is the equivalence relation generated by the defining equations and closed under those three arrow operations.

DosenPetric/PalomarCorrespondence.lean proves descent from terms to the quotient by Derives, restriction of full proof congruences to terms, pointwise relation correspondence, preservation of substitution closure and totality, correspondence of distinctness, and preservation by derived negation. The extension from a congruence closed under substitution to a full proof congruence uses the proved fragment dichotomy. The short proof uses occurrence isolation, ContextualCollapse.all_contexts and ShortProof.total with the q_A/e_A arrows. All quantification over parallel arrows preserves empty hom-sets, and repeated occurrences retain distinct tags. The metadata makes no priority claim or claim to an exhaustive novelty assessment. Full maximality contradicts source2007 nonmaximality conjecture; verify exact zero-identity Boolean category, nonempty variables and substitution-closed congruence. Metadata does not establish exhaustive novelty. Independently check correctness, novelty/priority and precise AI allocation against the pinned primary statement. The primary source reports: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the two research notes of the author's Erdős #81 series, in one package. Note I, "From realizability certificates to the Erdős 81 bound": a realizability certificate of Paper V for an auxiliary conflict system whose target is the physical system of copies of K₃ and K₄ in G (conflict when they share an edge, gain C(|K|,2) − 1), with q ≥ 1 classes and budget q·e(G) + cost ≤ q·T + w(X), gives a clique partition of G into pieces of order at most four with at most T pieces (note_I_partition_of_certificate; no chordality); a physical packing with e(G) − g(P) ≤ T does the same (note_I_partition_of_paid_packing); with a certified fractional optimum w, the far branch (e(G) − w < n²/6 − ηn², every η > 0, large n, no chordality) and the near branch (chordal, n ≥ 4·10¹², η = 10⁻¹⁶) give partitions with at most M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋ pieces (note_I_far_certificate, note_I_near_certificate); assembled through the transfer, every large chordal graph has such a partition (note_I_erdos81_eventual) and every chordal graph one with at most M(n) + b pieces for an absolute b (note_I_erdos81_all_orders). entry.description: Colorability and realizability defects in resource-dominated packing relaxations. The primary source reports: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of the author's preprint "Colorability and Realizability Defects in Resource-Dominated Packing Relaxations" (Erdős #81 series, Paper V). For a conflict system (finite objects with a symmetric irreflexive conflict relation) and a multiset X of objects, the loss between fractional and integral packings is bounded by the colourability defect D_q of the conflict graph H[X] of the copies (Lemma 3.1, Corollary 3.2, Theorems 3.3, 3.4, 3.4w), and, more generally, by the cost of a realizability certificate whose classes are realized in a fixed target system (Theorems 4.2 and 4.4). Applications: host completion through list edge colouring of bipartite multigraphs (Theorem 5.2: Galvin and Borodin–Kostochka–Woodall; Corollary 5.3; Example 5.5, a quadratic separation on K_{r,r}), the vertex-copy inequalities ν₃*(G_{v→u}) + ν₃*(G_{u→v}) ≤ 2ν₃*(G), ν₃(G_{v→u}) + ν₃(G_{u→v}) ≤ 2ν₃(G) + oct(H[T₂]) and ≤ 3ν₃(G) for triangle packings (Theorems 6.1, 6.2, Corollary 6.2a) and mixed triangle/K₄ copy inequalities (Theorem 7.3). Eighteen statements in all. Multisets are multiplicity functions X : O → ℕ and the conflict graph lives on the copies Σ o, Fin (X o). Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 take the optimum as an explicit maximizing point of a resource-dominated relaxation (a structure recording the resources, the feasible region inside the resource-capacity polyhedron and the characterization of its 0/1 points; convexity is not used) and assume all its coordinates are at most one. Theorem 4.4 and Example 5.5 state the realizability defect for the admissibility classes of identity and host realizers. In Corollary 5.3 the host system restricted to B has the triangles (e, h) with e ∈ B as objects. Theorems 6.2 and 7.3 (integral) hold for arbitrary maximum (maximum-weight) packings P' of G_{v→u} and P'' of G_{u→v}, given as feasible sets of the conflict systems: the multiset is their image in G (mappedTri, mappedMixed), each member of P' and P'' counted at its image under the copy map. ν₃* is a supremum over fractional triangle packings (registered definition), proved equal to the library's linear-programming form. entry.description: The ten minimum universal sets of MacMahon cubes. The primary source reports: A universal inventory of six-coloured MacMahon cubes can build a 2 by 2 by 2 model of every target variety, using eight distinct physical copies, without requiring internal face colours to match. We prove that the minimum inventory size is twelve and classify all ten labelled inventories attaining it, even when repetitions are allowed. They are exactly the two-triangle sets in Conway's tableau. The proof derives row and column sums of two from usability inequalities, proves symmetry, and eliminates every other degree-two inventory by corner coverage. Finite kernel-checked witnesses establish sufficiency. The formalization also verifies the proper cube rotations, outward faces, and completeness and uniqueness of the thirty geometric representatives. entry.description: Fluctuation bounds for first-passage percolation. The primary source reports: Only the newly reported lattice bound at one direction with a complementary-hyperplane quadratic expansion and its own constants is collected as a possible extension; the published main lattice/continuum fluctuation theorems are not new discoveries of this formalization. A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two papers of S. Armstrong and A. Bou-Rabee on the fluctuations of passage times in first-passage percolation. "Curvature and variance in lattice first-passage percolation": for independent, identically distributed edge weights on Z^d, d >= 2, whose law nu has an exponential moment and nu({0}) below the critical probability of bond percolation (Assumption (W)), and for constants delta in (0, 1], r > 0, Lambda >= 0 and lambda > 0, there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu(x)| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every unit vector xi in R^d, rational or not, at which the time constant mu has a quadratic expansion on the orthogonal hyperplane with these constants (Assumption (Curv): a linear term, a quadratic form at least lambda |h|^2, and a remainder at most Lambda |h|^(2 + delta) for |h| <= r), and every x in Z^d other than 0 within distance |x|^(3/4) of the ray through xi; epsilon and C do not depend on the direction (Theorem 1.1). The repository also proves the variance bound that follows, Var T(0, x) <= 2 C^2 |x|^(1 - epsilon), and Var T(0, floor(n xi)) <= n^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large integer n, uniformly in the direction, the floor taken coordinatewise. "Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation": for the random density psi(chi * W) of Gaussian white noise W on R^d, d >= 2, with chi smooth, radial and supported in the closed unit ball and psi continuous with values between two positive constants, the passage time T over rectifiable curves has a time constant mu = lim t^(-1) E T(0, t e_1), and there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu |x|| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every point x with |x| >= 1 (Theorem 1.1); the same holds for every density of white noise or of a homogeneous Poisson process that is jointly measurable, determined by the noise in the closed unit ball around each point, bounded between two positive constants and equivariant under rotations and translations (Assumption A, Theorem 1.2). The repository also proves the variance bounds that follow, Var T(0, t e_1) <= t^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large t and Var T(0, x) <= |x|^(1 - epsilon) for every point x with |x| sufficiently large. Every result of the literature that the proofs cite is stated and proved in the repository. entry.anchor_claim: The source reports: Only the newly reported lattice bound at one direction with a complementary-hyperplane quadratic expansion and its own constants is collected as a possible extension; the published main lattice/continuum fluctuation theorems are not new discoveries of this formalization. A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two papers of S. Armstrong and A. Bou-Rabee on the fluctuations of passage times in first-passage percolation. "Curvature and variance in lattice first-passage percolation": for independent, identically distributed edge weights on Z^d, d >= 2, whose law nu has an exponential moment and nu({0}) below the critical probability of bond percolation (Assumption (W)), and for constants delta in (0, 1], r > 0, Lambda >= 0 and lambda > 0, there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu(x)| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every unit vector xi in R^d, rational or not, at which the time constant mu has a quadratic expansion on the orthogonal hyperplane with these constants (Assumption (Curv): a linear term, a quadratic form at least lambda |h|^2, and a remainder at most Lambda |h|^(2 + delta) for |h| <= r), and every x in Z^d other than 0 within distance |x|^(3/4) of the ray through xi; epsilon and C do not depend on the direction (Theorem 1.1). The repository also proves the variance bound that follows, Var T(0, x) <= 2 C^2 |x|^(1 - epsilon), and Var T(0, floor(n xi)) <= n^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large integer n, uniformly in the direction, the floor taken coordinatewise. "Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation": for the random density psi(chi * W) of Gaussian white noise W on R^d, d >= 2, with chi smooth, radial and supported in the closed unit ball and psi continuous with values between two positive constants, the passage time T over rectifiable curves has a time constant mu = lim t^(-1) E T(0, t e_1), and there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu |x|| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every point x with |x| >= 1 (Theorem 1.1); the same holds for every density of white noise or of a homogeneous Poisson process that is jointly measurable, determined by the noise in the closed unit ball around each point, bounded between two positive constants and equivariant under rotations and translations (Assumption A, Theorem 1.2). The repository also proves the variance bounds that follow, Var T(0, t e_1) <= t^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large t and Var T(0, x) <= |x|^(1 - epsilon) for every point x with |x| sufficiently large. Every result of the literature that the proofs cite is stated and proved in the repository.

M02: one finite C>0 before every n>0 and origin-symmetric compact convex volume-one K with nonempty interior in maximal Gaussian measure position; its actual H0 Rayleigh infimum is at most C*n. M03: for each real P>=2 one finite C(P)>0 precedes every n>0, every even isotropic probability law nu satisfying the conventional compact-set IsLogConcaveMeasure condition, least Poincare constant at most P and finite actual Gaussian-relative Fisher information, and every origin-symmetric compact convex body D with nonempty interior supporting nu almost everywhere; lambda_1(interior D)<=C(P)*(n+sqrt(n*I(nu|gamma))). The log-concave density is derived from the law's original finite-information hypothesis; no density witness, covariance lower bound, ellipsoid-existence conclusion or desired spectral estimate is an additional premise. entry.description:
The orthogonal art gallery problem is ∃ℝ-complete (point-point and point-boundary), in Lean 4. The primary source reports: A Lean 4 formalization of material in a forthcoming manuscript entitled "The Orthogonal Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete". A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof, for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model, that deciding whether an orthogonal simple polygon (every edge horizontal or vertical) with rational corners can be guarded by g guards is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, both when the guards must see the whole polygon (point-point) and when they must see only its boundary (point-boundary). Both problems also reduce to ETR by formulas whose only variables are the 2g coordinates of the guards. As far as we could determine, hardness for orthogonal polygons was open: it is treated neither by Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow (J. ACM 2021) nor by Stade (SoCG 2025). The hardness proof is a new construction derived from Stade's polygon: needles become corridors, wedges become rectangles with needle cutters, the slanted mouths of the copy nooks are kept through helper guards pinned by four-armed crosses, and the addition gadgets are replaced by new orthogonal rooms. Its visibility, pinning and coverage facts are checked by the kernel as certificates (cone propagation with a symbolic height parameter, polynomial sign tests for the copy nooks, coverage by convex items). The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Direct AI involvement: {"methods": [{"method": "agent", "models": ["Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)"], "framework": "AI coding agents", "tool_setup": "Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) was used, as agents under the direction of the author, both for the Lean formalization and to assist with the documentation. The author set the task, the target statements and the requirements. Tools: Lean v4.35.0-rc2 and Lake, Mathlib, development programs with exact rational arithmetic (used to design and validate the construction and to generate its data and certificate files; not part of this repository), the toolchain's lake comparator and independent kernels.", "cost": {"wall_time": "not tracked", "spend_usd": "not tracked", "hardware": "cloud container"}, "prompting_notes": "n/a"}], "spend_usd": "not tracked", "notes": "The author directed the work. Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) assisted with the Lean definitions, statements, proofs, the development-time certificate generators (not part of this repository; the generated Lean files are checked by the kernel), and the documentation (README.md, this file, the Challenge.lean header, the notes in docs/ and the verification record). Reused files from the author's earlier entries are listed in docs/PROVENANCE.md."} Further checking: Check source/repository first-public chronology and overlap with the full corpus. - Machine model, polynomial time and reductions are those of PALOMAR-2026-10-02-000013: deterministic single-tape Turing machines over {blank, 0, 1, separator}, time = number of steps, polynomial bounds c * (n + 1)^k, polynomial-time many-one (Karp) reductions. ∃ℝ is the class of languages that reduce to ETR; invariance under other machine models is not proved.
- ETR formulas are quantifier-free formulas with constants 0, 1, operations +, −, · and relations =, <, ≤ under ¬, ∧, ∨, read existentially; variable indices are coded in unary. Art gallery instances are coded with numerators, denominators and g in binary.
- Polygons are lists of corners; simple means at least three distinct corners and any two distinct edges meeting exactly in common endpoints (collinear consecutive corners allowed); orthogonal means every edge is horizontal or vertical. The region is the boundary plus the bounded components of its complement; seeing means the closed segment lies in the region. The problems ask for a guard set with exactly g points, which is equivalent to at most g points since guards can be added.
- The orthogonal problems are not treated in the sources; AGPOrth and AGPOrthPointBoundary are the restrictions of the point-point problem of [AAM] and of the point-boundary problem of [S] to orthogonal polygons. Hardness is proved by a construction of our own (the forthcoming manuscript): Stade's polygon with every non-axis-parallel edge replaced, extra helper guards counted in the guard number, and a preprocessing step that replaces each constraint x = 1 by x · x ≥ 1 and x + x ≤ y with a fresh variable y.
- Stade's construction is formalized with explicit coordinates designed for the formalization rather than the coordinates of the paper. The hardness proof is a new construction derived from Stade's polygon: needles become corridors, wedges become rectangles with needle cutters, the slanted mouths of the copy nooks are kept through helper guards pinned by four-armed crosses, and the addition gadgets are replaced by new orthogonal rooms. - ETR formulas are quantifier-free formulas with constants 0, 1, operations +, −, · and relations =, <, ≤ under ¬, ∧, ∨, read existentially; variable indices are coded in unary. Art gallery instances are coded with numerators, denominators and g in binary.
- Polygons are lists of corners; simple means at least three distinct corners and any two distinct edges meeting exactly in common endpoints (collinear consecutive corners allowed); orthogonal means every edge is horizontal or vertical. The region is the boundary plus the bounded components of its complement; seeing means the closed segment lies in the region. The problems ask for a guard set with exactly g points, which is equivalent to at most g points since guards can be added.

Hardness is proved by a construction of our own (the forthcoming manuscript): Stade's polygon with every non-axis-parallel edge replaced, extra helper guards counted in the guard number, and a preprocessing step that replaces each constraint x = 1 by x · x ≥ 1 and x + x ≤ y with a fresh variable y.

entry.description: Half-rate prefix clocks for every two-input gate. The primary source reports: Rule 30's right edge, read in the frame that moves with it, is the map x_j -> x_j XOR (x_(j-1) OR x_(j-2)) on binary sequences. Its first n bits repeat with period 2^E(n), and the kit proves E(n) <= ceil(n/2) + Q_0(floor(n/2)), where Q_0 grows like an iterated logarithm (`Rule30RightPeriods.per_upper_half`). We prove that this upper bound does not depend on OR. Take any family of two-input gates g_j, one per depth, and any seed, finite or infinite, and let bit j evolve by x_j(t+1) = x_j(t) XOR g_j(x_(j-1)(t), x_(j-2)(t)), missing bits white. The exponent obtained by lifting one bit at a time is exactly that of the least period (`Rule30Submission.prefix_period_iff`), and every window of bits obeys the kit's record-charge bound E(a+2m) - E(a) <= m + Q_(E(a))(m) <= m + Q_0(m) (`Rule30Submission.prefix_window_bound`, `Rule30Submission.prefix_window_le_B`, `Rule30Submission.prefixExp_le_B`). If every gate is affine, the first n bits have period dividing 2^r whenever n + 1 <= 2^r (`Rule30Submission.affine_prefix_bound`). The reason is that a gate's derivative in its newer input is constant, s or NOT s, so one more finite difference removes it, and the kit's reset and countdown laws need nothing else. No lower bound, doubling density or statement about the centre column is claimed. Later same-package extension: For gates g_j, one per depth, and any seed, bit j of the edge map evolves by x_j(t+1) = x_j(t) XOR g_j(x_(j-1)(t), x_(j-2)(t)), missing bits white; with g = OR this is the right edge of Rule 30. Our earlier submission R30-20261030-7b0d12 proved that the first 2m bits have period 2^E(2m) with E(2m) <= m + Q_0(m), the kit's record-charge bound, which allows the excess E(2m) - m to reach 3 from m = 19. We prove it cannot do so before 2058: E(2m) <= m + 2 for every m < 2058, every gate family and every seed (`Rule30Submission.prefixExp_le_add_two`, `Rule30Submission.first_excess_three`). Three new laws hold for every gate: no three consecutive doublings once the period is at least 2 (`Rule30Submission.no_three`); after a pair whose second bit alone doubles, the next bit doubles exactly when the gate is quadratic and the pair's first bit has odd weight (`Rule30Submission.after01_double_iff`); and after two doublings from period M, the next bit's difference order is at least M - 2 (`Rule30Submission.after11_order`). Choosing the stretch after the last visit to excess 1 before excess 3 first appears, these force two countdowns, of the first bits' order and then of the last bits' resource, which cost at least 2058 pairs together. A computed family, found by search, attains excess 2 from m = 3. Nothing is claimed about excess 3 being reached, about later thresholds or about the centre column. Direct AI involvement: Primary submission credits Gareth Herbert; Claude (Anthropic); GPT (OpenAI); agent Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 Further checking: Partial bounded theorem only; no Rule30 Prize target solved. Combined earlier and later declarations in one package, not two counts. Check gate families/finite canonical windows/model-local step bounds and prior kit overlap. Head-Cone Locality, 2-Adic Transient Elimination, and Unconditional Step Lower Bounds for Prize Problem 3. The primary source reports: We formalize `Rule30Problem3Bounds` in core Lean 4.35.0 (~1.8 s, zero external dependencies), establishing the first structural lower-bound machinery and unconditional step-count lower bounds in the catalog for `Rule30Problem3.Machine`:

1. Head-Cone Locality & 2-Adic Transient Elimination (`run_eq_of_init_eq_lt`, `init_tape_eq_of_mod_two_pow_eq`, `computes_eq_of_mod_two_pow_of_run_le`, `computes_const_on_dyadic_ray`): In `t` steps from `head = 0`, `M.run n t` depends only on tape cells `0 <= i < t`. For any `k >= 1`, all inputs `m, n >= 2^(k-1)` with `m % 2^k = n % 2^k` share identical initial tapes on `i < k`. Thus if `Computes M f T` and `T n <= k` for even one input `n >= 2^(k-1)`, `f` is constant across the entire residue ray `{m >= 2^(k-1) | m % 2^k = n % 2^k}` down to `2^(k-1)`.
2. Residue-Flip, Blank-Reach, and Periodicity Bounds (`time_gt_of_mod_two_pow_ne`, `log2_succ_succ_le_time_of_ray_flip`, `evPer_two_pow_of_eventually_time_le`, `time_unbounded_of_problem1`): A single pair `r, m >= 2^(k-1)` with `r % 2^k = m % 2^k` and `f r != f m` forces `k + 1 <= T n` for all `n >= 2^(k-1)` in that residue class. When `L = Nat.log2 n + 1` and `f (n + u * 2^L) != f n`, `M` must take at least `Nat.log2 n + 2` steps. Bounded step time `T n <= k` for `n >= N` implies `eventuallyPeriodic`, so `Problem1` implies `T n >= k + 1` infinitely often for every `k`.
3. Fast Cone Evaluation & Unconditional Uniform Bounds (`center_eq_fastCenter`, `two_le_time`, `three_le_time`, `four_le_time`, `five_le_time`, `log2_succ_succ_le_time_lt_16`): Using `stepRow` on `rowAt 0 (-t) (2t + 1)`, we verify the residue-flip witnesses for `k = 1..4` (`t <= 99`) and prove unconditionally that every machine computing `center` satisfies `k + 1 <= T n` for all `n >= 2^(k-1)` (`1 <= k <= 4`) and `Nat.log2 n + 2 <= T n` for all `1 <= n < 16`. Later same-package extension: We formalize `Rule30Problem3WindowBounds` in core Lean 4.35.0, extending `Rule30Problem3Bounds` with word-level bitwise dyadic ray verification up to `k = 10` (`1024` rays) against `Rule30Window.centerBits` and finite canonical-window step lower bounds:

1. Word-Level Dyadic Ray Verification (`maskFlipsLoop`, `testBit_maskFlipsLoop`, `all_up_to_10_ok`, `exists_flip_in_canon_window`): Accumulating the bitwise XOR of the canonical window word `(centerBits >>> 2^(k-1)) % 2^(2^k)` against `11` period shifts certifies in a single kernel check that every canonical representative `r in [2^(k-1), 2^(k-1) + 2^k)` (`1 <= k <= 10`) flips within `11` period steps inside `windowN = 16384`.
2. Uniform Bounds up to `k = 10` & Blank-Reach for `n < 1024` (`time_ge_of_pow_le_ten`, `six_le_time`..`eleven_le_time`, `log2_succ_succ_le_time_lt_1024`): Every machine `M` computing `center` in time `T` satisfies `k + 1 <= T n` for all `1 <= k <= 10` and `n >= 2^(k-1)` (in particular `11 <= T n` for `n >= 512`), and `Nat.log2 n + 2 <= T n` for all `1 <= n < 1024`.
3. Finite Canonical-Window Periodicity & Lower Bounds (`period_of_canon_window_time_le`, `exists_canon_window_time_ge_le_thirteen`, `fourteen_le_max_time_window_4096`, `diagonal_canon_window_time_ge`): If `T r <= k` holds merely on the finite canonical window `[2^(k-1), 2^(k-1) + 2^k)`, then `f` has global period `2^k` from `2^(k-1)` onward. With `Rule30FactorWindow.transient_add_period_ge` this forces `k + 1 <= T r` on `[2^(k-1), 2^(k-1) + 2^k)` for every `k <= 13` (`14` steps on `[4096, 12288)`), and with `Rule30LeftUnbounded.D_period_unbounded` it gives for every `k` a left diagonal `D j` (`j <= 2^(2*2^k)`) forcing `k + 1 <= T r` inside `[2^(k-1), 2^(k-1) + 2^k)`. Kit pull request 69 (Troy Lowry, `Rule30EtherGrounding`) defines an ether $\mathrm{ether}(i,t)$ of period 4 in depth and 8 in time, and proves that no two adjacent depths of a black-edge code follow it eventually. Let $L(k)=\lfloor2k/3\rfloor+4-[k\equiv0,2\pmod{6}]$. For every code $x$ with $x_0=1$, every $k\ge1$, phase $(i,q)$ and onset $s$, bits $k$ and $k+1$ of $T^tx$ equal $\mathrm{ether}(i,t+q)$ and $\mathrm{ether}(i+1,t+q)$ on at most $L(k)$ consecutive ticks $t\ge s$ (an episode), and an explicit code $w$ attains $L(k)$, also when cut after bit $k+1$ (`Rule30Submission.episode_max`, `Rule30Submission.episode_bound`, `Rule30Submission.wit_episode`, `Rule30Submission.episode_witness_finite`). The kit has the frame (`Rule30FrozenRuler`) and a front-and-potential method for the period-three ether (`Rule30EtherThreeErosion`); we found no stated episode bound in the kit, its open pull requests or the submissions. Phillips (2004) explored periodic-background boundary growth experimentally. Left-Diagonal Anti-Periodicity and Unbounded Asymptotic Density-1/2 Diagonals for Prize Problem 2. The primary source reports: We formalize `Rule30LeftAntiPeriod` in core Lean 4.35.0 on top of `Rule30LeftReset`, `Rule30LeftUnbounded`, and `Rule30Prize`, establishing left-diagonal anti-periodicity and unbounded asymptotic density-1/2 diagonals for Prize Problem 2:

1. **Constant Parity & Period/Anti-Period Dichotomy (`par_const_of_periodic`, `D_period_or_antiperiodic`, `D_evAntiPer_of_not_evPer`, `D_evPer_or_evAntiPer_pow_whiteCount`):** Whenever `D j` has period `L` from `s` on, its length-`L` XOR parity `par (D j) t L` is constant for all `t >= s`. Thus when `D (j + 1)` is white from `s` on, `D (j + 2)` is either `L`-periodic (`par = false`) or `L`-anti-periodic (`D (j + 2) (t + L) = ! D (j + 2) t`, `par = true`). In particular, whenever `D (j + 2)` fails to have eventual period `L` while `D j` and `D (j + 1)` do, `D (j + 1)` is eventually white and `D (j + 2)` is eventually `L`-anti-periodic.

2. **Exact Period-`2L` Balance & `Problem2` Asymptotic Density 1/2 (`blackCountFor_add_two_mul_of_antiperiodic`, `natAbs_discrepancy_le_of_antiperiodic`, `halfDensity_of_antiperiodic`):** Every eventually `L`-anti-periodic sequence `f` contains `L` black cells in every `2*L` window after its transient `T`, bounding `|2 * blackCountFor f n - n| <= T + 2*L` for all `n >= T` and proving `HalfDensity f` (the exact `Rule30Prize.Problem2` density-1/2 condition).

3. **Infinitely Many Density-1/2 Left Diagonals (`D_antiperiodic_unbounded`, `D_halfDensity_unbounded`, `D_infinitely_many_halfDensity`):** Combining `D_period_unbounded` with `exists_step_break` proves that for every `L > 0` there is a left diagonal `D j` (`j <= 2^(2*L)`) with `EvAntiPer (D j) L`, `not EvPer (D j) L`, and `HalfDensity (D j)`, and for every `N` there exists `j > N` and `k` such that `D j` is `2^k`-anti-periodic with `HalfDensity (D j)`. Companion branch: `left-diagonal-antiperiod-density` (`f46738d`). Direct AI involvement: Primary submission credits G.P.J.W. entry.description:
Universal 010-Synchronizing Complement Waves, 2-Step Period-Doubling, and Mod-3 Shift-Template Laws in Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeCascade. The primary source reports: We extend `Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeCascade` in core Lean 4.35.0 with 10 universal (all-K, all-n) theorems governing `11`-free wave synchronization, 2-step period-doubling, and multi-step shift templates for `win3pow n = 3 * 2^n + 1`:

1. **Universal `010`-Synchronizing & `11`-Free Complement Laws (`no11_complement_propagation_step1`, `no11_complement_propagation_step0`, `sync_010_complement_step1`, `sync_010_complement_step0`):** For both `bstep1 K` and `bstep0 K`, `(false, true, false) = 010_2` is a 3-bit synchronizing word: if `(Y_s, Y_{s+1}, Y_{s+2}) = (false, true, false)` (`s >= 2`) and `Y` is `11`-free above `s + 2`, then `Z = bstep1 K Y` (and `bstep0 K Y`) locks into the bitwise complement `Z.testBit i = !Y.testBit i` with `(Z.testBit (i - 1) || Z.testBit i) = true` for all `i >= s + 2`.

2. **2-Step Period-Doubling & Type II Root Cascade (`nor_wave_B_shift_period6`, `typeII_step3_and_step4_cascade`):** Chaining `wave_100_to_011_step1`, De Morgan's law, and `wave_011_to_period6_step0` proves that `B_shift K Y` maps any `(100)^infty` NOR wave on `[m, K)` into the period-6 `(000101)^infty` wave (`(B_shift K Y).testBit (i + 6) = (B_shift K Y).testBit i` for `i >= m + 11`), so every Type II primitive root enters `(011)^infty` at step 3 and `(000101)^infty` at step 4.

3. **All-`n` Low-Bit Waves & Mod-3 Shift-Template Laws for `win3pow` (`bstep1_B_shift_win3pow_low_wave`, `B_shiftIter_two_win3pow_low_wave`, `bstep1_B_shift_win3pow_mod3_shift_13`, `B_shiftIter_two_win3pow_mod3_shift_13`):** For all `n >= 1` and `i < n`, step 3 of `win3pow n` has `testBit i = decide (i % 3 = 1)` and step 4 has `testBit i = decide (i % 3 != 1)`. Thus for `n = 2 + 3*m` (`13, 97, 769, ...`), both step 3 and step 4 (`B_shiftIter 2 K`) are exact `3*m`-bit shifts of `13` for all `d >= 0`. Companion branch: `stripe-cascade-sync` (`2b374fe`). 1. **Backward Period Descent & Two-Diagonal Period Bound (`D_evPer_pair_iff_all`, `D_pair_period_bound`, `D_white_period_bound`):** By `D j t = xor (D (j + 2) (t + 1)) (D (j + 1) t || D (j + 2) t)`, `D m` and `D (m + 1)` both have eventual period `Q` iff every `D i` (`i <= m + 1`) has eventual period `Q`. Thus `EvPer (D m) Q` and `EvPer (D (m + 1)) Q` (`Q > 0`) alone force `m + 3 <= 2^(2*Q)` (strengthening `D_common_period_bound`), and at any white diagonal `EvWhite (D (m + 1))`, `EvPer (D m) Q` forces `m + 3 <= 2^(2*Q)`.

2. **The 9-Diagonal White-Reset Neighborhood & Twin Density-`1/2` Diagonals (`D_white_prev_three`, `D_post_white_complement`, `D_post_white_no11`, `D_twin_antiperiodic_of_not_evPer`):** Around any white diagonal `D (j + 1)`, backward reconstruction gives `D (j - 2) t = xor (D j t) (D j (t + 1))` and `D (j - 3) t = D j t && ! D j (t + 1)` (`11`-free), while forward evolution forces `D (j + 3) = true`, `D (j + 4) (t + 1) = ! D (j + 2) t`, and `D (j + 5)` to be `11`-free. Hence whenever period `L` breaks at `D (j + 2)`, both `D (j + 2)` and `D (j + 4)` are `L`-anti-periodic with `HalfDensity`.

3. **Sharp Gap `5` Between White Diagonals, `whiteCount <= (j + 3) / 5`, and Right-Diagonal Density `1/2` (`D_white_gap_five`, `whiteCount_le_div_five`, `D_evPer_pow_div_five`, `R_infinitely_many_halfDensity`):** Any two eventually white diagonals `D a, D b` (`a < b`) satisfy `a + 5 <= b` (sharp at `D 2, D 7`), giving `whiteCount j <= (j + 3) / 5` (exact for `0 <= j <= 7`) and `EvPer (D j) (2 ^ ((j + 3) / 5))`; on the right, for every `k`, some `R j` (`k < j < 2^(k+1)`) is `2^k`-anti-periodic with `HalfDensity (R j)`. The 3-Level Backward Transducer State-Collapse Hierarchy: 010 Causal Firewalls, 00 Period-Doubling, and Universal 6L Period Bounds. The primary source reports: We extend `Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeCascade` in core Lean 4.35.0 with a 3-level state-collapse hierarchy for the 2-bit state `(Z_{i-2}, Z_{i-1})` of the backward operators `bstep1 K Y` and `bstep0 K Y`:

1. **Level 1 -- 1-State Collapse (`010` Causal Firewall & Exact Period Preservation):** For ANY window `Y` (with no `11`-free hypothesis), if `(Y_s, Y_{s+1}, Y_{s+2}) = (false, true, false)` (`2 <= s`, `s + 3 < K`), both `bstep1 K Y` and `bstep0 K Y` reset their 2-bit state at `(s + 2, s + 3)` to `(true, !Y_{s+3})` (`bstep1_010_state_reset`, `bstep0_010_state_reset`). Consequently, `010` erases all lower-bit differences below `s` (`bstep1_congr_of_010`) and preserves any period `L >= 1` on `[s + 2, K)` without period-doubling (`bstep1_periodic_of_010`), carrying the period-6 `(000101)^infty` wave to `(111010)^infty` (step 5) and `(001101)^infty` (step 6) (`wave_000101_to_111010`, `wave_111010_period6_step`).

2. **Level 2 -- 2-State Collapse (`00` Period-Doubling Bound):** Reading `(false, false)` fixes `(0, 0)` and merges `(0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)` into `(1, 1)` (`bstepTrans_00_collapse`), forcing `M^4 = M^2` (`iterPair_four_eq_two`) and bounding the backward preimage period of any `00`-containing `L`-periodic tail by `2 * L` on `[s + 2 * L, K)` (`bstep1_periodic_two_mul_of_00`).

3. **Level 3 -- 3-State Collapse (Universal `6 * L` Period Bound):** Reading any bit merges `(0, 1)` and `(1, 1)` (`bstepTrans_merge_true`), forcing `M^9 = M^3` (`iterPair_nine_eq_three`) and period `6 * L` on `[s + 3 * L, K)` for every `L`-periodic tail (`bstep1_periodic_six_mul`). Branch: `stripe-cascade-transducer-collapse` (`26925c4`). Direct AI involvement: Primary submission credits G.P.J.W. Consequently, `010` erases all lower-bit differences below `s` (`bstep1_congr_of_010`) and preserves any period `L >= 1` on `[s + 2, K)` without period-doubling (`bstep1_periodic_of_010`), carrying the period-6 `(000101)^infty` wave to `(111010)^infty` (step 5) and `(001101)^infty` (step 6) (`wave_000101_to_111010`, `wave_111010_period6_step`).

Finite-Vessel Tape Invariance, Box-Repeat Periodicity, and Non-Halting Propagation on Dyadic Rays. The primary source reports: We extend `Rule30Problem3Bounds` in core Lean 4.35.0 with unvisited-cell tape invariance, finite-box `[L, B)` configuration-repeat periodicity, and dyadic-ray non-halting propagation for one-tape Turing machines (`Machine`):

1. **Unvisited-Cell Tape Invariance & Left/Right Exterior Rays (`run_neg_steps_le_head`, `ScansAbove`, `scansAbove_neg_of_le`, `tape_eq_init_of_head_ne`, `tape_eq_init_of_scansBelow`, `tape_eq_zero_of_scansAbove`):** After `s` steps from `head = 0`, any active configuration satisfies `-(s : Int) <= c.head`. If cell `i : Int` is never visited before step `t`, then `c.tape i = (M.init n).tape i`. Consequently, under `ScansBelow M n t B` every cell `i >= B` equals `(M.init n).tape i`, and under `ScansAbove M n t L` (`L <= 0`) every cell `i < L` is blank (`0`).

2. **Finite-Box Agreement & Repeat Periodicity (`tape_eq_all_of_box_eq`, `run_periodic_of_box_repeat`):** If the head stays inside `[L, B)` up to `t_1 + p` and the configurations at `t_1` and `t_1 + p` agree on `state`, `head`, and the finite box `L <= i < B`, they agree on all of `Int` and `M.run n (t_1 + d + k * p)` has the exact same `state`, `head`, and `tape` as `M.run n (t_1 + d)` for all `k, d : Nat`.

3. **Permanent Spatial Trapping & Dyadic Ray Non-Halting (`not_halts_and_trapped_of_box_repeat`, `not_halts_dyadic_ray_of_box_repeat`):** Any finite-box repeat (`0 < p`) forces non-halting and `[L, B)` confinement for all `t : Nat` across the entire dyadic ray `m % 2^B = n % 2^B` (`m, n >= 2^(B-1)`). entry.description:
Exact Conjugacy Between Rule30SurvivalBridge Frontier Scans and Rule 30 Left Diagonals. The primary source reports: We establish an exact conjugacy between the autonomous frontier scan `pureScan` of `Rule30SurvivalBridge` and the Rule 30 left diagonals `D j` (`Rule30Diagonals`, `Rule30LeftUnbounded`, `Rule30LeftAntiPeriod`) in core Lean 4.35.0:

1. **Exact `(true, true)` Diagonal Frontier Conjugacy (`scanStep_diagMem_succ`, `pureScan_diagFrontier`, `iterPureScan_diagFrontier`):** Defining `diagFrontier q r` with `k`-th symbol `diagSym q k = (D (2 * k + 1) (q + k + 1), D (2 * k) (q + k))`, each `scanStep` applies `D_step` twice, yielding `pureScan (diagFrontier q r) = diagFrontier (q + 1) r` and `iterPureScan n (diagFrontier q r) = diagFrontier (q + n) r` for all `n, q, r : Nat` with zero transient.

2. **Exact `(true, false)` Branch Conjugacy (`scanStep_diagMemFalse_succ`, `pureScan_diagFrontierFalse`, `iterPureScan_diagFrontierFalse`):** On the `(true, false)` branch, `diagFrontierFalse q r` shifts diagonal indices by one (`(D (2 * k + 2) (q + k + 2), D (2 * k + 1) (q + k + 1))` after `(true, false), (false, true)`), satisfying `iterPureScan n (diagFrontierFalse q r) = diagFrontierFalse (q + n) r` for all `n, q, r : Nat`.

3. **Terminal Scalar Field `FG` & Unbounded Periods (`diagFrontier_terminal_FG`, `diagFrontier_not_evPer`):** Along any successful run from `diagFrontier q (r + 1)` with `r + 2 <= n + k`, `FG (window tape) (r + n - k) 0` equals `(D (2 * k + 1) (q + n + k + 1), D (2 * k) (q + n + k))`, and `iterPureScan` realizes arbitrarily large minimal periods. The source reports: We establish an exact conjugacy between the autonomous frontier scan `pureScan` of `Rule30SurvivalBridge` and the Rule 30 left diagonals `D j` (`Rule30Diagonals`, `Rule30LeftUnbounded`, `Rule30LeftAntiPeriod`) in core Lean 4.35.0:

1. **Exact `(true, true)` Diagonal Frontier Conjugacy (`scanStep_diagMem_succ`, `pureScan_diagFrontier`, `iterPureScan_diagFrontier`):** Defining `diagFrontier q r` with `k`-th symbol `diagSym q k = (D (2 * k + 1) (q + k + 1), D (2 * k) (q + k))`, each `scanStep` applies `D_step` twice, yielding `pureScan (diagFrontier q r) = diagFrontier (q + 1) r` and `iterPureScan n (diagFrontier q r) = diagFrontier (q + n) r` for all `n, q, r : Nat` with zero transient.

2. **Exact `(true, false)` Branch Conjugacy (`scanStep_diagMemFalse_succ`, `pureScan_diagFrontierFalse`, `iterPureScan_diagFrontierFalse`):** On the `(true, false)` branch, `diagFrontierFalse q r` shifts diagonal indices by one (`(D (2 * k + 2) (q + k + 2), D (2 * k + 1) (q + k + 1))` after `(true, false), (false, true)`), satisfying `iterPureScan n (diagFrontierFalse q r) = diagFrontierFalse (q + n) r` for all `n, q, r : Nat`.

3. **Terminal Scalar Field `FG` & Unbounded Periods (`diagFrontier_terminal_FG`, `diagFrontier_not_evPer`):** Along any successful run from `diagFrontier q (r + 1)` with `r + 2 <= n + k`, `FG (window tape) (r + n - k) 0` equals `(D (2 * k + 1) (q + n + k + 1), D (2 * k) (q + n + k))`, and `iterPureScan` realizes arbitrarily large minimal periods.

entry.description: A proof of the Murty–Simon conjecture on diameter-2-critical graphs. The paper reports: Das and Fox report that every n-vertex diameter2-critical graph has at most floor(n²/4) edges for every n, with equality only for the balanced complete bipartite graph. This removes the previous enormous sufficiently-large-n restriction. Their maximal-matching lemma bounds edges outside any maximal matching by nonedges. Direct AI involvement: The primary paper explicitly says GPT-5.6 Sol found the full bound and even-n equality on August11. Authors simplified the bound and supplied an all-n equality argument, wrote the paper themselves, then made minor GPT-6 Astra feedback edits. Further checking: Verify the full all-n edge bound and uniqueness equality proof against the prior sufficiently-large-n theorem. Paper credits GPT-5.6 Sol with the bound and even-n equality; odd-n equality is the authors’ new argument. August11 is reported private discovery, not first public release; use arXiv October28. The November1 formalization is the same package, not a second result. Independently check the exact formal scope and author-independent replay. entry.description: A counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture. The paper reports: Ren reports a division-ring extension H⊂T with iterated bimodule right-dimension sequence(1,2,2,...) and infinite left H-dimension, built from nearest-neighbour quantum Laurent fraction rings with parameter1/2. The paper concludes that the triangular ring(H,T;0,T) is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, disproving the stated pure semisimplicity conjecture. Direct AI involvement: The primary paper directly credits GPT-6 Astra with choosing the criterion and developing the main proof, especially the division rings T and H_r. The author reports checking every proof and completing Lean formalization and editing with GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus5.5. Verify whether the Lean main theorem covers the full ring-theoretic conclusion or only its criterion; inspect all hypotheses and statement correspondence.
